### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/driver-sql`, `@objectstack/driver-turso`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/objectql`, touching **40** documentable anchor(s).

**11** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/data-modeling/drivers.mdx`  _(via SqlDriver (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/index.mdx`  _(via SqlDriver (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/queries.mdx`  _(via SqlDriver (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`  _(via needs_confirm (literal, a string literal in diffManagedTable; a string literal in isPublishedColumnChange), relax_not_null (literal, a string literal in diffManagedTable; a string literal in isPublishedColumnChange))_
- `content/docs/kernel/cluster.mdx`  _(via ensureObjectStorage (symbol, a method of class ProtocolRegistryHydrationFacet))_
- `content/docs/permissions/tenant-audit-census.mdx`  _(via SqlDriver (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/plugins/packages.mdx`  _(via SqlDriver (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/index.mdx`  _(via SqlDriver (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/lifecycle.mdx`  _(via SqlDriver (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/query-syntax.mdx`  _(via SqlDriver (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx`  _(via SqlDriver (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **4** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via SqlDriver (symbol, a top-level class), needs_confirm (literal, a string literal in diffManagedTable; a string literal in isPublishedColumnChange))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via DriftOp (symbol, a top-level type), SqlDriver (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via SqlDriver (symbol, a top-level class), registerExternalObject (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-1.mdx`  _(via SqlDriver (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 80 pages)`
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **37** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bfbcd81fbaa2f7b4d6c65e896d98b80cbd891133` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `3b86c1557556dd629ab3bbc091f2da91a34ed45a` — the merge of head `b67fa33af4da5520152063c2297d09baed5c0241` into base `bfbcd81fbaa2f7b4d6c65e896d98b80cbd891133`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 3b86c1557556dd629ab3bbc091f2da91a34ed45a && git checkout 3b86c1557556dd629ab3bbc091f2da91a34ed45a
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin bfbcd81fbaa2f7b4d6c65e896d98b80cbd891133 b67fa33af4da5520152063c2297d09baed5c0241 && git checkout -B drift-repro bfbcd81fbaa2f7b4d6c65e896d98b80cbd891133 && git merge --no-ff b67fa33af4da5520152063c2297d09baed5c0241

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bfbcd81fbaa2f7b4d6c65e896d98b80cbd891133
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs bfbcd81fbaa2f7b4d6c65e896d98b80cbd891133` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

The diff widens the published surface as the `exports` maps decide it: `ObjectQL.applyPublishedColumnChanges` (@objectstack/objectql "."), `SqlDriver.applyPublishedColumnChanges` and the `DriftOp` member `widen_date_to_datetime` (@objectstack/driver-sql "."), the optional `MetadataHostEngine.applyPublishedColumnChanges?` (@objectstack/metadata-protocol "."), and the wire advisory rule `object-column-changes-not-applied`. Nothing is removed or tightened.
- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is now declared at line start in the changeset and the PR body. `clause2-line.mjs` reads it as yes/widening.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` holds: `storage.notNull: false` and `date`→`datetime` keep their already-declared meaning, and only enforcement changes.
- No `packages/spec/src/**` file and no governed path is touched. The spec `syncObjectSchema` contract (`data-engine.ts:637`) is unchanged and still holds.
- Delta review of round-1 findings: the must-fix (declaration) and the should-fix (Postgres `lock_timeout`, 5 s, SET LOCAL, 55P03 → skipped + advisory) are both fixed on this head. The delta adds no surface.

### ② Semver level

- `patch` on all four packages is correct (AGENTS.md step 3: "a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch`").

### ③ Boundary flags

- Destructive refusal intact: 409 `DESTRUCTIVE_CHANGE` at save, and `allowDestructive: false` at publish.
- ADR-0113 D5: the explicit-false relax stays `needs_confirm`, the boot never applies it, and an absent `storage.notNull` is never relaxed.
- Remaining nits go to one follow-up card: the D5 wording, the unbounded MySQL MDL wait, the cli.mdx classification row, the Turso REMOTE end-to-end pin, MySQL COMMENT loss on `MODIFY`, and the Postgres re-read taken under the lock.
- PR author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (relay); no third-party login.
